newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Kingfisher shares up as profits soar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Kingfisher shares up as profits soar.

text.p: By Jane Merriman LONDON - British stores group Kingfisher on Wednesday sent its shares soaring with record annual profits powered by strong sales and market share gains from do-it-yourself arm B&Q, electricals chain Comet and Woolworths.

The retailer's 36 percent increase in profits to 390.2 million pounds ($620.4 million), topped market expectations and this pushed its shares up strongly. They stood 18 pence higher at 692.5 by 1027 GMT. Sales rose 10 percent to 5.81 billion pounds.
The company was confident that its range of retail businesses would ensure growth could be sustained in the future.
Chief executive Sir Geoffrey Mulcahy told Reuters in an interview, "If you look to the future we believe we are well placed in growth markets."
Improved operational performance, plus a more buoyant consumer climate helped its retail chains boost sales and market share.
"All of Kingfisher's main businesses increased sales and improved their shares of their key markets," Mulcahy said in a statement.
But he said the group needed to continue to improve efficiency and boost sales by keeping pace with customers changing needs because of increasing competition.

He declined to comment on speculation in the British press that Kingfisher might need to make an acquisition to drive growth in the future and could be interested in buying stores put up for sale by rival retailer Littlewoods.
"What we say is that we're very much focused on markets for the home and family...and the clear priority is to build our businesses in the UK and France and concentrate on doing just that."
He said Kingfisher's B&Q and French unit Darty were both market leaders in DIY and electricals respectively and that these were forecast to be relatively high growth markets.
Comet was a strong number two in the British electricals market, where demand for home computers was expected to continue growing.

Mulcahy said it was too early to comment on sales in the current year. But when asked if uncertainty ahead of Britain's May 1 general election had affected overall consumer demand he said consumers were already cautious about spending.
"I think consumers are cautious anyway," he said, "you have to offer them real value and real service and real choice if you're going to encourage them to spend money."

Improved operational efficiencies helped the group's performance last year. Mulcahy said B&Q made improvements in its supply chain and more than achieved a 20 million pounds cost saving target identified a year ago.
Woolworths increased market share in toys, home essentials and home entertainment.
"I think Woolworths has demonstrated over the years that it is capable of continually improving the offer its makes to its customers," he said, "and achieving growth in the markets we've targeted."
He said chemist chain Superdrug was meeting its objectives in terms of the returns from stores which have been revamped.
Darty, the French electricals business, had done well in a difficult market. But Mulcahy said Kingfisher believed there were early signs that the market was improving.

Mulcahy said the group was getting to know French furnishing and electricals retailer BUT, in which it bought a 26 percent stake last year. The deal included a two year standstill agreement on Kingfisher increasing its stake.
($ = 0.628 British Pounds)
